c.tagline: A turquoise coast beneath ancient ruins.

avoid.reason: Resort scams — inflated bar bills, carpet/timeshare touts; drink-spiking in nightlife

hood_desc: The charming walled old town of Antalya with Ottoman-era houses, narrow lanes, boutique hotels and a picturesque marina. Ideal for travelers who love historic atmosphere and seaside character.
A modern resort strip east of the center known for sandy beaches, large all-inclusive hotels and spas. Best suited to beach-focused holidaymakers wanting sun and resort comforts.
A long pebble-and-sand beach district backed by the Beydaglari mountains, with promenades, parks and family attractions. Great for beachgoers who want scenic mountain-meets-sea views.
The lively central district of Antalya covering the modern downtown, shopping and everyday city life. Suits visitors who want to stay near urban amenities and transport.
An upscale golf and beach resort area east of Antalya famed for luxury hotels and championship courses. Perfect for golfers and travelers seeking high-end all-inclusive stays.

water.note: Tap water is treated but bottled or filtered water is recommended for visitors.

transit.pay: Cash is not accepted on board: use an Antalyakart smart card, sold and topped up at kiosks and machines at tram stops, the airport and the bus station, or pay by tapping a contactless bank card on buses and trams (slightly higher fare). Rides cost well under US$1.
transit.hours: The AntRay tram and city buses run roughly 6am to midnight; dolmuş minibuses are frequent during the day.
